# workflow-checks

Three small programs that do the checking a back-office person does by hand, and show their evidence for every call.

**Live sample outputs: https://jacobmetoyer.com/workflow-checks/** (generated by running the code below on its sample data)

> **Synthetic data, not deployed for any client.** Every company, person, patient, account and amount in this repository is invented by a seeded generator. These are demos of an approach, not products, and no savings or accuracy figures are claimed for real data.

## What each check catches

| Demo | Who it is for | It catches | You get |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Freight packets](freight_packets/README.md) | Carrier and broker billing / settlement staff | Billable detention from geofence or tracking times (free time, grace, increments, caps); late arrivals; carrier invoice lines that don't match the rate con (linehaul, fuel, accessorials, totals); duplicate invoices; missing POD; carrier fines backed by evidence, with a 7-day dispute window | One draft packet per load with the calculation and evidence timeline, `invoice_flags.csv`, `settlement.csv` (READY / HOLD and net payable), an exception queue |
| [PT authorizations](pt_auth/README.md) | Authorization specialists at multi-clinic outpatient PT groups | Scheduled visits outside any approved auth; completed visits with no auth; re-auths due by visits-left or days-left per payer rule; pending auths with visits coming up; annual visit caps; unknown payers | A prioritized daily worklist (P1/P2/P3) with submit-by dates and the payer's checklist, a printable digest, an auth ledger |
| [Utility bills](utility_watch/README.md) | AP staff paying utility bills across a multifamily portfolio | Usage spikes against the same month last year (so seasonal swings aren't flagged), rate jumps, duplicate bills, overlapping periods, missing bills, late fees, payment mismatches, unpaid past-due bills, usage at vacant units | `flags.csv`, an exception queue, a payment-approval queue (nothing is paid), a one-file HTML report |

Every decision is written to an append-only `audit.jsonl` with a `file:row` pointer to the input that caused it. Anything the rules can't judge goes to a person, not a guess.

## Run it in 60 seconds

Needs Python 3.10+. The demos use only the standard library; `pytest` is for the tests.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Jacob-Met/workflow-checks && cd workflow-checks
cd utility_watch && python -m uwatch run --data sample_data --out out --as-of 2026-09-28 && cd ..
# open utility_watch/out/report.html
cd freight_packets && python -m freightpkt run --data sample_data --out out && cd ..
# open freight_packets/out/packets/*.html, or browse it: python -m freightpkt serve --data sample_data --out out  (http://127.0.0.1:8765)
cd pt_auth && python -m ptauth run --data sample_data --out out --as-of 2026-09-28 && cd ..
# open pt_auth/out/digest.html, or: python -m ptauth serve --data sample_data --out out  (http://127.0.0.1:8766)
```

Tests (130 in total):

```sh
pip install pytest
(cd freight_packets && python -m pytest -q)
(cd pt_auth && python -m pytest -q)
(cd utility_watch && python -m pytest -q)
```

On Windows PowerShell, `.\demo.ps1 freight|pt|utility|test` does the same. `python scripts/build_pages.py` runs the tests and rebuilds the sample outputs site in `docs/`.

## How it is built

- **Synthetic data only.** Seeded generators write an independent answer key (`expected.json`) that the tests check against.
- **Deterministic rules first.** Anything uncertain goes to a human exception queue, and nothing is sent, filed, paid or submitted.
- **No paid APIs, no network calls, no model calls.** The local UIs are single pages with no CDN and bind to 127.0.0.1.

## What the tests do and do not show

- **They show internal consistency.** Each generator writes the synthetic data and an `expected.json` answer key from the same seed, and the tests check the engine against that key plus hand-written edge cases (see each `HARDENING.md`). A green run means the rules do what the README says on data built to exercise them.
- **They do not show real-world accuracy, savings or time saved.** No result here was measured on a real company's exports, so none is claimed. Any figure in a demo script (for example a detention total) is a property of the synthetic sample, not a typical or expected result.
- **A real pilot starts from a baseline.** The per-PoC READMEs list what a pilot needs: the client's own exports, their real rules, and a manual audit to compare against. Claims about a pilot would be limited to what that comparison measured, for that client and period.

## Status, support and contributions

- **Demos, provided as-is.** No warranty, no support commitment and no maintenance schedule. They are not production software and must not be pointed at real patient, financial or personal data as they stand (see `pt_auth/README.md` for the HIPAA gaps).
- **Not accepting outside contributions** for now. Issues may be read but are not guaranteed a reply.
- **Licensed under the MIT License** (see [`LICENSE`](LICENSE)). The runtime has no third-party dependencies; `pytest` (MIT) is a test-only dependency and is not distributed here.
